items.name: ETA 2824-2
items.summary: The archetypal Swiss workhorse automatic. Robust, easy to service and used by dozens of brands for decades, it is the reference point that most other mid-range movements are compared against.

items.name: ETA / Valjoux 7750
items.summary: Designed by Edmond Capt and introduced in 1974, the cam-lever 7750 is the most widely used automatic chronograph movement in the world, and the base of countless modified calibres.

items.name: ETA F06.111
items.summary: One of the most common Swiss quartz movements: inexpensive, thin and reliable, found in many affordable Swiss-made watches.

items.name: Grand Seiko 9R65
items.summary: A Spring Drive movement: a mainspring powers the gear train, but instead of an escapement a glide wheel generates a little electricity to drive a quartz-controlled electromagnetic brake. The result is a perfectly smooth seconds hand.

items.name: Miyota 8215
items.summary: A simple, durable and very affordable automatic that has powered entry-level mechanical watches for decades.

items.name: Miyota 9015
items.summary: A slim, high-beat Japanese automatic often used as an alternative to Swiss calibres in affordable and micro-brand watches. It is known for a noisy, "wobbly" rotor.

items.name: Omega 8800
items.summary: A Master Chronometer calibre with Omega's co-axial escapement and silicon balance spring, resistant to magnetic fields of 15,000 gauss and certified by METAS.

items.name: Rolex 3235
items.summary: Rolex's modern date calibre, featuring the Chronergy escapement, a blue Parachrom hairspring and a 70-hour power reserve. Each cased watch is tested to −2/+2 seconds per day.

items.name: Seiko 7S26
items.summary: The movement inside the SKX family and older Seiko 5s, built around Seiko's efficient "Magic Lever" winding system. It neither hacks nor hand-winds, but is famous for running for decades without attention.

items.name: Grand Seiko 9F61
items.summary: The benchmark high-accuracy quartz movement. Hand-selected, aged crystals, thermocompensation, a backlash-free seconds hand and a twin-pulse motor make it arguably the finest analog quartz movement in production.

items.name: Seiko NH35A
items.summary: The supplier version of Seiko's 4R35. It is cheap, tough and easy to regulate, which has made it the default engine of micro-brands and the watch-modding community.

items.name: Sellita SW200-1
items.summary: Developed after ETA restricted supply to brands outside the Swatch Group, the SW200-1 is dimensionally compatible with the 2824-2 and powers a large share of today's Swiss mid-range watches.

items.name: ETA / Unitas 6497
items.summary: A large, open pocket-watch movement with a slow 18,000 vph beat. Ideal for skeletonising and very popular for learning watchmaking because its big parts are easy to see and handle.

items.name: Zenith El Primero 400
items.summary: Announced in 1969, the El Primero was one of the first automatic chronograph movements and the first high-beat one. Its 36,000 vph frequency lets it time events to a tenth of a second.
